messages:
alex (customer): hey team — since ~09:20 UTC our streaming requests are failing. Client sees ECONNRESET / broken pipe and we get 502s in our sidecars. upstream model completes but users get truncated responses and they're being billed. ticket: https://support.example.com/INC-6231

maria (support): thanks alex — sorry about the hit. can you share an example x-request-id and a repro curl? also we need timeframe + region

alex (customer): sure — x-request-id=req_20260317_8201, region=us-west-2, timeframe=09:20-09:45 UTC. repro: we call the streaming endpoint with chunked encoding, client sends keepalives, then sometimes client suddenly drops. curl example:

```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-1","stream":true,"prompt":"hello"}'
```

we saw this log on our proxy:

```
[proxy] 2026-03-17T09:21:02Z conn=12345 read: client reset (EPIPE)
[rt-gateway] request=req_20260317_8201 status=502 note="upstream finished but client closed"
```

alex (customer): billing flagged it as 5xx for the whole request and charged full tokens. invoice id INV-9987

maria (support): copying eng-sre and billing. tim / jen can you triage?

tim (eng-sre): looking. initial read: gateway treats unexpected client half-close as a server-side failure because our streaming handler returns 5xx when it fails to finish sending chunks. if upstream finished generating and we successfully flushed final chunks but TCP half-close from client happened during write, our current heuristic counts it as a 5xx. we should differentiate client abort (499-ish) vs gateway error.

jen (billing): if we confirm these were client disconnects, we should credit the affected tokens. need list of request ids and timestamps. alex can you confirm any other req ids?

alex (customer): also saw this pattern on three other reqs: req_20260317_8210, req_20260317_8243

tim (eng-sre): thanks. repro attempt: I ran a quick local replay against gateway with simulated client close mid-stream — I can reproduce broken-pipe + 502 classification. Log excerpt:

```
[gateway] write_chunk err=write: broken pipe 
[metrics] request=req_20260317_8201 result=5xx reason="write failure to client"
```

but the model returned full tokens to the gateway. we should change counting to mark "client aborted" and exclude from 5xx billing. patch idea: detect TCP ECONNRESET/EPIPE and set response_code=499; update metering pipeline to not bill tokens for 499.

maria (support): timeline/next steps?

tim (eng-sre): immediate mitigation: add a heuristic that if upstream completion time < 5s before client close and gateway saw final chunk flushed, mark as client-abort. i can push a hotfix to staging, then to canary in us-west-2 for 30m. longer term: add explicit half-close signalling in our streaming protocol and update metering backend.

jen (billing): ok once eng provides list of affected req ids we can process credits. will need approximate token counts from logs.

repro-bot: automated replay ran against req_20260317_8201 -> reproduced broken-pipe on iteration 4/10, exit code ECONNRESET. attached trace id TRACE-77-A

alex (customer): appreciate it. can you also add a note to the account so our finance sees the followup?

maria (support): done — added internal note INC-6231 with action items: (1) eng to deploy heuristic canary (tim) (2) billing to queue credits (jen) (3) support to notify customer with ETA.

tim (eng-sre): pushing canary now to us-west-2. will post rollback criteria. monitoring queries I used:

```sql
-- count write errors where upstream finished
SELECT count(*) FROM gateway_logs WHERE err LIKE '%broken pipe%' AND upstream_status='complete' AND ts > '2026-03-17T09:00:00Z';
```

maria (support): ETA for canary?

tim (eng-sre): canary up in ~12m. I'll watch error rate and token-metering deltas. if errors drop or classify as client-abort we proceed to 1hr global rollout. rollback if client-visible 5xx increases > 1% for the canary slice.

jen (billing): I'll start drafting a credit run for req_20260317_8201/8210/8243 pending eng confirmation of token counts.

alex (customer): thanks — will wait for the update.

maria (support): keeping this thread updated. assigning P0 label until billing processed. :eyes:
